rows.title: CT still borrowing to pay off debt, but some are pushing back
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s budget calls for $80M in new borrowing in the next two years to pay off existing debt, but some say the practice should end.

rows.title: CT legislators raising questions about heating assistance program
rows.standfirst: Legislators want to know how many families can’t get any more funding from the Connecticut Energy Assistance Program.

rows.title: Report shows pandemic, inflation left CT hospital finances reeling
rows.standfirst: A new report from the CT Hospital Association shows the pandemic and inflation left CT hospital operating margins well below pre-COVID levels.

rows.title: Lamont defends truck mileage tax: ‘You got to pay your bills’
rows.standfirst: A GOP bill up for a public hearing Friday would end collection of CT’s truck mileage tax on July 1. The tax raised $4.3 million in January.

rows.title: CT essential state workers awarded $45M in pandemic relief
rows.standfirst: A labor arbitrator has awarded bonuses of about $1,200 to CT public sector workers, with payments ranging based on a job’s risk level.

rows.title: State money for heating assistance unspent; deadline extended
rows.standfirst: Gov. Lamont extended the deadline for LIHEAP assistance, but state funds for relief remain unspent. Critics say the state was too frugal.

rows.title: CT comptroller seeks solutions to municipal pension fund crisis
rows.standfirst: The surging costs of the CT Municipal Employees Retirement System are pressuring towns, and the comptroller wants to preserve the program.

rows.title: Report: Taxing the rich won’t make them leave CT
rows.standfirst: A Better Connecticut Institute, a progressive policy group, released an analysis showing tax policy has little impact on household migration.

rows.title: Legislators wary of extending CT income tax cut to the richest
rows.standfirst: The Lamont administration’s plan to cut CT income taxes is still alive, but both Republican and Democratic lawmakers fear going too far.

rows.title: CT treasurer: Don’t change the unclaimed property program yet
rows.standfirst: Legislation could increase the amount of money returned to CT residents, but treasurer Erick Russell says his office is already overwhelmed.

rows.title: CT budget panel approves essential worker relief for state employees
rows.standfirst: CT legislators endorsed nearly $50 million in pandemic bonuses for state workers, but Republicans want more hero pay for the private sector.

rows.title: CT hasn’t spent millions budgeted for health care, human services
rows.standfirst: CT legislators and labor are asking if the administration is making progress fixing a staffing crisis and responding to health care needs.
